prompt: Which two questions does the lesson use to tell BI tools apart?

choices.text: Which charts it draws and how fast
choices.why: Every tool draws a bar chart; features tell you little.
Right. The four tools sit at four different answers.

choices.text: Its price and its logo colour
Which cloud company owns it, and which country hosts its servers
choices.why: Not the axes the lesson uses.

prompt: Match each tool to who builds in it.
Which two of the four tools does this course run on your machine?

choices.why: Both are commercial and not run.
Right. Open source, at opposite corners.

choices.text: Tableau Public and Metabase Cloud, because they are the free ones
choices.why: Neither is run, and Metabase Cloud is paid.

prompt: In Tableau, what happens when you drag a field onto Rows?

choices.text: It writes, runs and draws a query
choices.why: Right. A chart is a query drawn.

choices.text: It copies the field into a spreadsheet
It asks you to write the SQL for the chart
It creates a new table in the database with the field's values, ready for other tools
choices.why: It reads; it does not create tables.

prompt: Tableau classified `order_id`, stored as a number, as a measure. What goes wrong?

choices.why: An id identifies; adding ids means nothing.
Right. The tool guessed from the type, and a guess is a definition nobody chose.

prompt: Match each Tableau term to the term lesson 4 used for the same idea.
Why is Tableau Public the wrong place for Lantern's customer data, even invented?

choices.why: Right. Fine for open data; wrong for anything a company would not put on a billboard.

prompt: Match each LookML element to what it describes.

pairs.right: one table, its dimensions and measures
which views may be joined, and how
a group of explores and the connection

prompt: In the LookML view, what does `primary_key: yes` buy beyond labelling a column?

choices.text: It creates an index in PostgreSQL
choices.why: LookML does not change the database.
Right. Looker uses it to compute sums correctly where a join would repeat rows.

choices.text: It hides the column from users
It makes the column a measure, summed by default in every explore that includes the view

prompt: A job advertisement asks for experience with LookML. Which product does it mean?

choices.why: It has no LookML; it was Google Data Studio.
Right. The enterprise platform with a central model.

choices.text: Power BI, which compiles LookML into DAX when a model is published

prompt: Why does `type: sum` on a LookML measure close lesson 4's implicit-measure problem?

choices.why: A sum of the wrong column is wrong.
It allows them, defined by the modeller.

choices.text: The modeller chooses it once, so explorers cannot pick another
choices.why: Right. Nobody exploring it picks an average by accident.

choices.text: Because it converts reais to cents

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer an editor question to a SQL question where the editor suffices?

choices.why: Right. It cannot offer a SQL question's columns as filters to other people.

choices.text: The editor gives more accurate sums than SQL written by hand, because it checks the grain
choices.why: Both send SQL to the same database.

prompt: Why did Metabase's editor not offer the customer's segment under `Orders`?

choices.why: It can; the grants cover the schema's views.
Right. Metabase cannot know `orders.customer_id` points at `customers` until told in Table Metadata.

choices.text: Metabase only joins tables in the Sample Database
choices.why: It joins any table it knows a key for.

prompt: What is the office segment's net revenue over the whole period, in reais?
The SQL Metabase wrote joins `orders` to `customers` with a `LEFT JOIN`. Why is that join safe for the sum?

choices.text: It goes from the fact to a dimension with one row per key
choices.why: Right. Each order meets one customer, so no order is repeated.

choices.text: Because the sum is computed before the join
Because Metabase runs it twice and compares the answers

prompt: What is a Metabase model?

choices.text: A saved question treated as a table
choices.why: Right. Joins and columns done once, then queried like a table.

choices.text: A machine-learning model trained on the data
A dashboard template that other teams import, with its filters already wired
choices.why: That is not what Metabase calls a model.

prompt: A colleague builds a Metabase metric that filters out refunded orders by itself. What is wrong?

choices.why: They can; that is the trouble here.
Right. The layer already decides refunds; a second decision in the tool brings lesson 2's meeting back.

choices.text: Refunded orders should be included in revenue
Metrics must be written in SQL

prompt: Match each definition to where the lesson says it belongs.

pairs.left: which rows count as net revenue, and which day an order falls on
a metric named for Metabase's menu

prompt: A group can open a collection but not query the data behind a question in it. What happens when they open the question?

choices.why: Right. Collection and data permissions combine.

choices.text: Metabase grants them data access automatically

prompt: What does the lesson say about public links in the Metabase version it runs?

choices.why: That is what makes them public: they do not.

choices.text: Public sharing starts enabled; turn it off for customer data
choices.why: Right. A link is publishing, and revoking it does not unsee what was seen.

prompt: Why does the most generous data permission inside Metabase still stop at the schema `semantic`?

choices.text: Its role reads only the layer
choices.why: Right. Lesson 3's role is the ceiling, whatever Metabase grants.

choices.text: PostgreSQL hides other schemas from every remote client by default, for every role
choices.why: It does not; the role's grants decide.

prompt: Why is Streamlit installed into a virtual environment?

choices.text: What you install cannot disturb the rest of the machine
choices.why: Right. Its own copy of Python's libraries, in one directory.

choices.text: To hide the app from other users on the machine and from the browser

prompt: How many megabytes did the virtual environment take after installing Streamlit and psycopg?
Why does the app get a role of its own instead of reusing `metabase`?

choices.text: PostgreSQL allows one tool per role
Each tool reads only what it needs, revocable on its own
choices.why: Right. This role reads two views.

choices.text: Streamlit requires a role whose name starts with its own

prompt: You remove *home* from the selector. What does Streamlit do?

choices.text: Changes only the chart, without running anything

choices.why: Right. Every interaction runs the script from the top.

choices.text: Reloads the page from the server's cache without any Python running
choices.why: Python runs on every interaction; only the query may come from the cache.

prompt: Why is the password in `.streamlit/secrets.toml` and not in `app.py`?

choices.text: Streamlit cannot read strings from Python files
So the program travels without the password
choices.why: Right. And the secrets file never goes into version control.

choices.text: TOML files are encrypted by Streamlit

prompt: In the app's query, the segments are passed as `%s` rather than pasted into the SQL. What does that prevent?

choices.text: A value being read as part of the SQL
choices.why: Right. A parameter is sent beside the query, never as code.

prompt: What does `gatherUsageStats = false` in `config.toml` do?

choices.text: Stops Streamlit sending usage statistics to its company
choices.why: Right. It does so by default.

choices.text: Turns off the database's statistics collector, which speeds up every query

prompt: The app's metric with both segments reads the same total as the layer. What is it, in reais?
You edited `app.py`, started Streamlit again, and the browser still shows the old app. Why?

choices.text: The first app still holds 8501, and the new one took 8502
choices.why: Right. 8502 is not forwarded; stop the old one and start again.

prompt: `streamlit: command not found` — what is the fix?

choices.why: It is already installed, in the environment.

choices.text: Run it as root with sudo

choices.why: Right. Or activate the environment first.

prompt: You break the password in `secrets.toml` and the app keeps showing numbers. Why?

choices.text: Streamlit ignores secrets after the first run
choices.why: It reads them on each connection.

choices.text: PostgreSQL accepts any password from localhost
The cached answers are still within their ten minutes
choices.why: Right. A cache hides a broken source for exactly as long as its time to live.

prompt: Put the steps of getting the app running in order.
items: create the environment and install Streamlit

prompt: Which question does the lesson say teams forget when choosing a BI tool?

choices.text: Which tool draws the best charts

choices.why: Right. The people who build it may leave in a year.

choices.text: Whether it has a dark mode
How many connectors it lists on its website

prompt: There is no budget for licences. Which tools does the lesson point to?

choices.text: Power BI, because Desktop is free
Looker Studio and Tableau Public, which both keep data private by default

prompt: Why can a company that keeps its definitions in database views change BI tool without changing a number?

choices.text: Because every BI tool computes sums the same way
choices.why: They do, but each can sum different things.

choices.text: No tool was allowed to decide what the numbers mean
choices.why: Right. The new tool reads the same columns of the same views.

choices.text: Because views export themselves to the new tool's format
Because the new tool imports the old tool's dashboards

prompt: Where can a definition of net revenue hide, outside the database, according to this lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A Metabase metric with its own filter
The SQL inside a Streamlit app
choices.why: Right. The app is the code.
It holds connection details, not definitions.
